---
title: "Creating presentations with Quarto"
---

Quarto can also turn a `.qmd` file into a slide deck. Presentations use the same YAML header and Markdown body as the
reports covered in the previous tutorial; they simply render slide-by-slide instead of page-by-page.

**Do:** Take the Quarto report that you started working on at the `documents` tutorial. Do you think you could turn it into a slideshow just by changing the `format` field in the YAML header, or would you need to rewrite the file from scratch?

**See:** Switching formats is again very simple at the YAML level. In practice you probably want to reorganize the content itself, since a slide holds much less text than a page, and each heading needs to mark where a new slide begins.

## Presentation Formats

| **Format** | **Output Type** | **Strengths** | **Challenges** |
|----|----|----|----|
| `revealjs` | HTML slides | Flexible; supports transitions, incremental reveals, embedded code. | Web-based only; needs attention to screen layout. |
| `pptx` | PowerPoint | Easy to share; editable after rendering. | Limited styling and dynamic features. |
| `beamer` | PDF slides (LaTeX) | High-quality, printable; ideal for academic talks. | Complex LaTeX configuration; limited interactivity. |

## Example: A Reveal.js Presentation

- [Example .qmd file](https://github.com/open-stat-prog/reproducible-reporting/blob/main/assets/docs/presentation_example.qmd)
- [Resulting .html output](https://open-stat-prog.github.io/reproducible-reporting/assets/docs/presentation_example.html)

Each slide begins with a heading (e.g., `##`) or is separated by `---`. When rendered, Quarto executes any embedded code
chunks and displays their output, such as tables or plots, directly on the slide.

Keep slides concise: aim for clarity, minimal text, and meaningful visuals rather than dense explanations.

**Common challenges:**

- **Balancing detail and readability:** avoid overloading slides with text or long code blocks.
- **Consistent design:** use concise titles and uniform font sizes.
- **Cross-platform compatibility:** check that revealjs slides display correctly across browsers; `pptx` output can
  render differently depending on the software used to open it.

As with reports, revealjs slides are HTML output, so if you're submitting or sharing slides as a single file, apply the
same `embed-resources: true` setting covered in the previous tutorial.

## Practice Exercise

:::: {.panel-tabset}
## {{< var tab_title.question >}}

You have a Quarto HTML report analyzing exam scores and want to present the same analysis as a revealjs slideshow that
you can safely email as a single file. What would you change in the YAML header, and what else would you likely still
need to adjust in the body of the document?

## {{< var tab_title.solution >}}

In the YAML header, change `format: html` to `format: revealjs` and keep `embed-resources: true` so the slideshow stays
a single, portable file. In the body, you would still need to reorganize the content into slide-sized chunks, adding
headings or `---` separators to mark where each new slide begins, and trimming dense text down to the key points.

::::
